sentences.text: The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 to 3 in CC No.2419/2017 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Chavakkad, a case which arose out of a protest complaint by de facto complainant.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Chavakkad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against them are under Sections 406 and 420 IPC read with Section 34 IPC.
In the present petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C, the petitioners seek to quash the proceedings in the said case.
2. Earlier, the Guruvayoor Temple Police had conducted an investigation in this case, on the basis of a complaint preferred by the 3rd respondent/de facto complainant.
After completion of the investigation, the police referred the case by filing a refer report stating that the issue involved is of civil nature.
3. It is thereafter that the learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence upon a protest complaint preferred by the de facto complainant/3rd respondent.
The matter was referred to the Ernakulam Mediation Centre for making an effort for amicable settlement of the issue between the parties.
The learned Mediator has filed a report dated 24.03.2025, along with Memorandum of Mediation Settlement 2025:KER:31496 Agreement, stating that the issue has been amicably settled between the parties.

The de facto complainant/3rd respondent also filed an affidavit before this Court stating that, in accordance with the terms of the mediation settlement, the petitioners had paid the outstanding amount to her, and hence she has no objection in quashing the proceedings against them.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant/3rd respondent, and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. The issue involved in this case relates to the non-payment of the balance amount of remuneration to the de facto complainant in connection with the interior work done in a building, as per the instructions of the petitioners.
Apparently, the dispute is thus of private nature.
Now, it is seen that the issue has been amicably settled between the parties, and the de facto complainant is not having any subsisting grievance against the petitioners.
In the above circumstances, the continuation of the prosecution proceedings against the petitioners can only be termed as an abuse Rajagopalan vs The Sub Inspector Of Police, Chavakkad ...
